findings.evidence: The theorem body only calls `isCompact_univ.elim_finite_subcover` and builds a cover via `mem_iUnion.2`. No `ImplicitAtlas` term appears in the statement.
findings.fix: Either restate it to give the atlas (e.g. `∃ C : Finset A, ∃ hC, P (𝒜.reindex (Embedding.subtype _) hC)`, or add a `finiteSubatlas` def alongside it), or rename it after its conclusion, e.g. `exists_finset_iUnion_footprint_map_eq_univ`.
findings.issue: `exists_finite_subatlas` concludes `∃ C : Finset A, ⋃ I : Finset C, 𝒜.footprint (I.map (Embedding.subtype _)) = univ`. That is only a covering condition, not an atlas, so the name claims more than the statement proves.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Data/Finset/Image.lean:258 `noncomputable def equivMap : s ≃ s.map f`. The same Tau Ceti file names its product equivalence `MulEquiv.piFinsetUnion`, after `Equiv.piFinsetUnion` (Mathlib/Data/Finset/Basic.lean:641).
findings.fix: Put `pi` in the name, e.g. `Finset.mapPiMulEquiv` (keeping the Finset namespace for dot notation on `I`), and rename `mulEquivMap_apply` and `restrict₂_mulEquivMap_symm` to match.
findings.issue: `Finset.mulEquivMap` reads as a multiplicative version of Mathlib's `Finset.equivMap : s ≃ s.map f`. It is actually the product relabelling `((α : I.map f) → π α) ≃* ((β : I) → π (f β))`, which is the `piCongrLeft` pattern.

findings.evidence: `private theorem kuranishiZeroSet_reindex` (line ~61) and `theorem kuranishiZeroSet_reindex_eq ... := kuranishiZeroSet_reindex (s := 𝒜.kuranishi) f I J`. Both state the same equality.
findings.fix: Name the public simp lemma `kuranishiZeroSet_reindex`, and inline or rename the private helper (e.g. `kuranishiZeroSet_reindex_aux`).
findings.issue: The public lemma `kuranishiZeroSet_reindex_eq` has an extra `_eq` suffix only because the private helper `kuranishiZeroSet_reindex` took the plain name. This breaks the pattern of its siblings `regLocus_reindex`, `kuranishi_reindex`, `footprint_reindex`.

summary: Names in the reindexing API mostly match their conclusions, but `exists_finite_subatlas` claims a subatlas where it only gives a covering finset, and `Finset.mulEquivMap` borrows the name of the unrelated `Finset.equivMap` for a product equivalence. One public lemma also carries a redundant `_eq` suffix.
